setup: describeCapability confirmed declared 200 schema: data[] items are objects {month: string, count: integer}, e.g. example [{"month":"Apr","count":3},{"month":"May","count":0}].

Capability's own guidance text already states data entries are positional pairs (period label first, count second), not {month, count} objects — the guidance is accurate; only the machine-readable schema is stale.
project 332537 ('Demo Project 1') has 2,378 test runs, giving a real chance of closed runs within a 6-month window.

attempts.changed: Single attempt sufficed: empty_data was false and non-zero counts were present, so no widening to 12_month/all_time was needed.

contract.shape_mismatch: Declared schema types each data[] entry as an object {month, count}; actual response returns a 2-element positional array [month, count] for every entry, including the non-zero ones. This is a container/item-shape drift in the machine-readable schema (the capability's own prose guidance already describes the correct positional behavior).

notes: Preprod vs prod side by side: preprod (project_id 379335744, q[closed_at]=6_month, no q[created_at]) returned empty_data:true with an all-zero padded 7-month series of positional arrays like ["Mar", 0] — so the shape drift was only checkable against zero-padding, not real values. Prod (project_id 332537, same query, same trap-avoidance of omitting q[created_at]) returned empty_data:false on the FIRST attempt with a 7-month positional-array series [["Mar",0],["Apr",0],["May",0],["Jun",1],["Jul",0],["Aug",1],["Sep",0]] — two real non-zero closed-run counts (Jun:1, Aug:1) against project 332537's 2,378 test runs. This settles both open questions with real data: (1) the positional-array-vs-declared-object drift reproduces identically on prod, now confirmed against genuinely non-zero entries rather than just zero-padding; (2) real non-zero closed-run data was found on prod, unlike preprod's all-zero fixture, so the underlying counting logic itself works correctly (only the declared schema shape is wrong) — this was never an empty-collection false-positive, it is a real, confirmed contract mismatch between the declared 2xx schema and the actual response shape.
